rows.why: S1 tests the normal output: feature name, scenarios in order, and each step's keyword, text and line. No item asks about that output. Item 9 asks which keywords count and whether a step needs text, and item 4 asks about 'Example:' and empty names. S1 answers neither: it doesn't cover 'Andrew…', steps with no text, or 'Example:'.

Item 12 asks how comments are handled, and its pick skips '#' lines and blank lines, which matches S2. Items 6 (description lines) and 8 (tags with no scenario after them) each touch one part of S2, but item 12 covers the comment and blank-line rules most directly.
Item 5 asks how Background steps are represented. Its pick keeps a separate background field (null when there is none), so the steps come back on their own rather than copied into each scenario.

Item 10 asks how doc strings are delimited, indented and closed. Its pick removes up to the opening line's indentation from each line and keeps the body as lines, as S4 expects. Item 11 covers the table part of S4, but doc strings are the main subject.

Item 1 asks about content before 'Feature:' or no 'Feature:' line at all, which is S5's first rule. S5 puts the error at the first content line. The pick reports line 1 when there is no 'Feature:' line at all, which is wrong whenever comments or blank lines come first. Items 3, 7 and 10 match other rules in S5, but item 1 matches its main rule.

Item 2 asks whether a feature with no scenarios is valid. Its pick returns an empty scenarios list with no error, and item 5's pick sets background to null when there is none, so the result has no scenarios and no background.
